title: ADK Finance Assistant
overview: A two-agent finance education assistant that combines sample budget analysis with delegated investment research. Google ADK coordinates OpenAI models through LiteLLM, while public search results retain source links and retrieval timestamps.
features: Root finance agent delegates public research to an investment planning agent.
Clearly labeled sample monthly budget supports educational savings conversations.
Search responses preserve public source URLs and UTC retrieval timestamps.
Atomic SQLite admission limits requests and model calls across local processes.
Local ADK web and command-line entry points support interactive sessions.
role: I integrated OpenAI-backed ADK agents, public search tools, local admission controls, and configuration diagnostics.
challenges: Keeping educational budget data separate from personal accounts and preventing search snippets from being presented as verified current prices or rates.
impact: I integrated two ADK agents to OpenAI, timestamped public-source research, and shared SQLite request admission.

title: Google Maps MCP & OpenAI Agent
overview: A Google ADK project comparing direct Google Maps function tools with a hosted Maps MCP integration. OpenAI handles the conversation, while the direct tool path supports route summaries and a places search near one route midpoint.
features: Separate agents demonstrate direct REST function tools and hosted MCP tool discovery.
Directions tool returns distance, duration, and a Google Maps route link.
Places tool searches within 5 km of one driving-route midpoint and returns up to five results.
CLI and ADK web interfaces share configuration and safe error handling.
Offline checks exercise tool fixtures; live Maps access requires separately configured Google Maps credentials.
role: I integrated OpenAI reasoning to direct Maps tools and an MCP agent, with configuration checks and bounded API requests.
challenges: Separating model access from Maps permissions and explaining that midpoint search covers one area rather than the entire route.
impact: I implemented two ADK integration paths for location tools: direct Maps REST functions and hosted MCP tool discovery.

title: ADK Shopping Assistant
overview: A conversational shopping demo that guides visitors from product discovery to a validated cart and order summary. Four Google ADK agents handle the conversation while Python controls catalogue prices and totals; Redis restores each browser’s shopping session.
features: Four specialist agents guide profile collection, catalogue browsing, checkout, and order summaries.
Python validates products and quantities and calculates cart totals from a fixed demo catalogue.
Streamed responses show progress while the assistant completes each turn.
Redis-backed browser sessions restore the conversation and cart after reload.
Uses made-up contact details; no payment is collected or real order placed.
role: I integrated four ADK agents with deterministic catalogue and cart tools, a streamed browser interface, Redis session recovery, and guarded API requests.
challenges: Maintaining consistent state between agent handoffs while ensuring the model cannot invent products, prices, or completed purchases.
impact: Connects product discovery, cart calculation, and checkout in one conversation. A live synthetic checkout verified 2 × ₹70,000 = ₹1,40,000 and an accurate demo order summary; no sales or conversion results are claimed.

title: Healthcare MCP & OpenAI
overview: An educational MCP server and OpenAI client for exploring illustrative healthcare records through structured tools. The client discovers tools dynamically and uses a bounded tool-calling loop over a local SQLite database.
features: FastMCP exposes four tools over Streamable HTTP.
Tools provide database schema, bounded SQL queries, patient risk summaries, and readmission insights.
Read-only SQLite connections and a SQL authorizer restrict database access.
Row limits and query execution budgets bound generated SQL work.
Rule-based summaries make the demo's scoring signals inspectable.
role: I integrated an OpenAI tool-calling client to MCP data tools, schema discovery, and restricted SQLite querying.
challenges: Bounding model-generated SQL and distinguishing illustrative rule-based risk signals from clinically validated predictions.
impact: I exposed four structured MCP tools through Streamable HTTP and bounded model-generated SQLite queries with read-only access.

title: Symposium RAG · Semantic Cache
overview: A document-grounded symposium assistant with persistent exact and semantic answer caching. Visitors ask about a fictional event guide and receive answers with page references; repeated questions can reuse a source-preserving cached answer.
features: A public browser chat answers questions about a fictional, contact-free symposium PDF.
OpenAI embeddings and FAISS retrieve guide passages for grounded answers.
Exact and semantic cache lookups retain the original source references.
The hosted Upstash Redis cache shares entries across serverless requests.
Shared request admission and controlled errors bound the public demo.
role: I integrated PDF retrieval, source-page references, persistent semantic caching, shared request admission, and the deployed browser interface.
challenges: Choosing similarity thresholds and isolating cached answers by source index while keeping the app usable without a Valkey service.
impact: Reuses grounded answers across repeated questions. Live checks confirmed a cache hit with source references and a refusal for absent information; production cost savings and hit rates have not been measured.

title: Symposium PDF RAG Bot
overview: A focused PDF question-answering assistant for a symposium guide. A responsive browser chat connects to a FastAPI retrieval service, combining OpenAI answers with inspectable page references for schedules, event rules, and registration.
features: Separate PDF ingestion builds a FAISS index of overlapping source passages.
Retrieval supplies relevant guide excerpts to the answer prompt.
Answers show deduplicated source-page references in expandable chat details.
Index metadata checks help detect a source or embedding mismatch.
Shared Upstash admission limits requests before provider work.
role: I integrated PDF ingestion, retrieval, answer generation, page-reference display, public API admission, and Vercel delivery.
challenges: Keeping the vector index aligned with its source document and prompting the model to acknowledge information absent from the supplied excerpts.
impact: Turns a five-page guide into a searchable conversation backed by 9 indexed passages. The live date-and-venue question returned the correct event details and page references; no user-adoption metrics are available.

title: Banking Agent Harness
overview: An interactive mock-banking assistant with deterministic Python controls around model-selected tools. Visitors review a staged transfer, confirm it in a separate turn, and inspect tool outcomes while a Redis-backed session retains their isolated demo ledger.
features: Five banking tools operate on synthetic beneficiaries, balances, and transfers.
Python validates beneficiaries, amounts, balances, and daily limits.
A staged transfer requires explicit confirmation in a later turn.
Tool outcomes and account balances show whether a mock action actually executed.
Redis-backed, isolated browser sessions preserve the demo ledger; no real money moves.
role: I integrated the ADK agent with deterministic policy, confirmation state, mock transaction execution, usage limits, and audit controls.
challenges: Preventing model instructions from bypassing confirmation and ensuring changed transfer details invalidate stale pending state.
impact: Keeps action approval in deterministic application code. A live ₹250 mock transfer left the balance unchanged until a separate confirmation, then reduced it by exactly ₹250; no real banking integrations or financial outcomes are claimed.

title: Agentic AWS Resource Management
overview: A learning project adapted from sanjayssnit's agentic AWS resource management repository. A Streamlit chat interface connects FastAPI and Claude tool calls to AWS Cloud Control operations and CloudWatch log queries.
features: Claude selects structured AWS tools through the Anthropic SDK.
Implemented Cloud Control handlers support resource creation requests, reading, and listing.
Create responses expose an asynchronous request token rather than confirmed resource completion.
CloudWatch tooling retrieves a bounded set of Lambda error log events.
FastAPI connects the tool loop to a Streamlit conversation interface.
role: I adapted and organized an existing AWS agent demo, retaining its original history and documenting setup, supported handlers, and verification limits.
challenges: Distinguishing advertised tool operations from implemented handlers and asynchronous creation requests from completed AWS resources. Update and delete handlers are not implemented.
impact: I adapted the AWS agent demo and documented its implemented Cloud Control create, read, and list handlers and bounded log queries.

title: Multi-Agent Customer Support
overview: A Streamlit support proof of concept that combines model-assisted information gathering with deterministic billing and refund specialists. LangGraph routes validated ticket state, while a separate approval graph handles eligible mock refund reviews.
features: Multi-turn information gathering compacts customer input into a validated ticket.
LangGraph routes billing, refund, and general support requests.
Specialist handlers use read-only SQLite tools and deterministic response templates.
A separate approver view resolves queued mock refunds and updates the customer session.
Upstash admission limits provider usage; customer sessions and approvals remain in process memory.
role: I integrated conversational intake, validated ticket state, specialist routing, human review, and session-aware approval outcomes.
challenges: Keeping the customer interaction responsive while a separate review workflow resolves a refund, with explicit boundaries around process-local session state.
impact: I separated conversational ticket intake from deterministic support specialists and a separate approval graph for mock refund reviews.

title: AI Voice Adventure Assistant
overview: A browser-based voice storytelling assistant that turns a spoken story idea into a written and spoken adventure. FastAPI coordinates transcription, contextual OpenAI generation, and speech synthesis, with a bundled demo recording so visitors can try the complete flow immediately.
features: Browser recording, audio upload, and a bundled demo recording provide multiple input paths.
Transcription, contextual reply generation, and speech synthesis run as a staged async workflow.
Bounded in-memory conversation history supports follow-up turns and session reset.
Recording duration, file formats, and upload sizes are constrained.
Manual playback remains available when the browser blocks audio autoplay.
role: I integrated browser audio capture to an asynchronous transcription, generation, and speech playback flow with recoverable errors.
challenges: Coordinating three provider stages, committing conversation state only after success, and handling browser recording and autoplay behavior.
impact: Completes audio input → transcript → contextual story → playable MP3 in one interface. The deployed demo completed all three provider stages and played the generated reply; physical microphone recording was not tested in this review.

title: Hybrid RAG Documentation Assistant
overview: Docwise is a documentation assistant that combines keyword and semantic search to answer technical questions with traceable sources. The hosted Python application fuses BM25 and MiniLM ONNX vector results through reciprocal rank fusion before generating a cited answer.
features: Two Markdown documents provide 39 heading-aware indexed passages.
BM25 keyword search and MiniLM ONNX embeddings combine through reciprocal rank fusion.
Answers include validated source labels and expandable retrieved passages.
Unsupported questions return an explicit documentation boundary.
FastAPI validates inputs and Upstash Redis enforces shared public-demo limits.
role: I integrated structure-aware ingestion, hybrid retrieval, citation validation, the Docwise browser interface, and a lightweight ONNX deployment for Vercel.
challenges: Preserving code context during chunking and combining keyword precision with semantic recall while keeping source labels tied to retrieved chunks.
impact: Makes 39 passages across 2 documents searchable with inspectable citations. Live checks verified a FastMCP answer against its retrieved passage and a refusal for an unrelated question; retrieval accuracy and business impact have not been benchmarked.

title: AI Support Ticket Classifier
overview: A FastAPI and LangGraph ticket-classification demo that converts free-text support requests into validated categories and team assignments. The pipeline includes pattern-based PII redaction, a model-based injection check, structured output validation, and a human-review fallback.
features: Browser interface submits tickets and displays structured classification results.
LangGraph sequences redaction, injection checking, classification, validation, and fallback handling.
Pydantic constrains output across seven issue categories and five teams.
Failed or unsafe classifications return a review-oriented fallback.
Atomic Upstash admission runs before provider work and returns retry information when requests are limited.
role: I integrated model configuration, schema-constrained classification, redaction and injection checks, API admission, and the browser demo.
challenges: Keeping untrusted ticket text separate from system instructions and returning predictable structured results when model output or provider access fails.
impact: I integrated ticket redaction, injection checks, schema validation, review fallback, and atomic provider admission in a LangGraph API.
